name: taxable_profit_elasticity
label: Taxable profit elasticity
description: Elasticity of the taxable profit base with respect to the net-of-tax rate (1 − t). Captures profit shifting, timing and real responses that change declared profits.
rationale: Devereux, Liu & Loretz (UK CT returns 2001-08; abstract) estimate an elasticity of taxable income of 0.14-0.18 for companies around the £300k kink and 0.54-0.57 around the £10k kink. The OBR's March 2021 costing of the 19%→25% rise (supplementary release, Table 1.1) cuts the 2025-26 static yield by 6% for profit shifting (semi-elasticity 0.65, 0.38 effective) and 10% for all behaviour, which this model reproduces with ε ≈ 0.19 and ε ≈ 0.32 respectively. Central 0.20; the range spans the small-company estimate.

name: user_cost_elasticity
label: User cost elasticity of investment
description: Long-run percentage fall in business investment for a 1% rise in the user cost of capital (σ).
rationale: Chirinko (2008, J. Macroeconomics 30(2), abstract): 'the weight of the evidence suggests a value of σ in the range of 0.40-0.60'. With a CES technology σ equals the long-run user cost elasticity of capital. Central 0.60 sits at the top of that range; the high end of 1.0 covers Cobb-Douglas.

name: profit_gdp_elasticity
label: Profit-GDP elasticity
description: Percentage change in the taxable profit base for a 1% change in the GDP level (η); drives dynamic revenue.
rationale: Team judgement: no citable estimate found, so the range was widened from the 9.5 prior. Unit elasticity assumes the taxable profit base moves in proportion to GDP.

name: behavioural_first_year_share
label: Behavioural response in year 1
description: Share of the long-run taxable-profit response that occurs in the first fiscal year.
rationale: Team judgement: no citable estimate found, so the range was widened from the 9.5 prior. OBR's 2021 costing note reports behaviour by year but no phasing parameter.

name: receipts_first_year_share
label: Receipts in year 1
description: Share of the first year's change in liabilities received as cash in that fiscal year (instalment timing).
rationale: HM Treasury Budget 2021 policy costings (p.20, CT main rate to 25% from April 2023): +£11,900m in 2023-24 vs +£16,250m in 2024-25, a first-year ratio of 0.73. That ratio also contains a smaller first-year behavioural response, so it is an upper bound on the cash-timing share; central 0.6 kept, high 0.75 covers it.

name: investment_adjustment_speed
label: Investment adjustment speed
description: Share of the remaining gap to long-run investment closed each year (λ, partial adjustment).
rationale: Team judgement: no citable estimate found, so the range was widened from the 9.5 prior.

name: main_rate_profit_share
label: Share of receipts from main-rate profits
description: Share of onshore CT receipts paid on profits taxed at the main rate; the rest is small profits and marginal relief.
rationale: HMRC Corporation Tax statistics 2026 (Figure 8, 2024-25 CT chargeable by rate): main rate £77.5bn, marginal relief £9.0bn, small profits rate £2.9bn, so the main rate is 77.5/89.4 = 0.87 of the total.

name: real_required_return
label: Real required return
description: Real discount rate (r) used in the user cost of capital and the present value of capital allowances.
rationale: Hanappi (2018), OECD Taxation Working Paper 38, Tables 1-A/1-B (p.19): real interest rate 5.00% in scenario 1 and 2.00% in scenario 2 (pre-tax real return p = 20%). Central 5%; low widened to 2%.

name: full_expensing_coverage
label: Full expensing coverage of P&M
description: Share of plant & machinery investment eligible for full expensing; the rest gets the 18% main-pool WDA.
rationale: Team judgement: no citable estimate found, so the range was widened from the 9.5 prior. HMRC guidance limits full expensing to companies' new, unused main-rate plant and machinery (no cars, no assets bought to lease); special-rate assets get a 50% FYA. The Autumn Statement 2023 costing (p.22) does not publish the qualifying share.

name: allowance_pv_intangibles
label: PV of allowances for intangibles
description: Present value of tax relief per £1 of intangible investment (intangibles regime and R&D relief).
rationale: Team judgement: no citable estimate found, so the range was widened from the 9.5 prior. Reflects relief at accounting amortisation or 4% a year plus R&D relief.

name: capital_share
label: Capital share of output
description: Output elasticity with respect to the capital stock (1 − labour share).
rationale: ONS 'Trends in the UK labour share: 1997 to 2023' (main points): labour share 59.5% of GVA at factor cost in 2023, so the capital share is 0.405. Central 0.40, range 0.35-0.45.

name: share_plant_machinery
label: Investment share: plant & machinery
description: Share of business investment in plant & machinery (incl. transport and ICT equipment).
rationale: Team prior from MASTER_PROMPT 9.5; awaiting a citable source.

name: share_structures
label: Investment share: structures
description: Share of business investment in non-residential buildings and structures.
rationale: Team prior from MASTER_PROMPT 9.5; awaiting a citable source.

name: share_intangibles
label: Investment share: intangibles
description: Share of business investment in intellectual property products.
rationale: Team prior from MASTER_PROMPT 9.5; awaiting a citable source.

name: depreciation_plant_machinery
label: Depreciation: plant & machinery
description: Annual economic depreciation rate of plant & machinery (δ_pm).
rationale: Team judgement: a standard Devereux-Griffith input that could not be verified against a primary source. The range is widened to the OECD explanatory annex (Table A.4), which uses 12.6% for industrial machinery to 37.0% for computer hardware.

name: depreciation_structures
label: Depreciation: structures
description: Annual economic depreciation rate of structures (δ_st).
rationale: Team judgement: a standard Devereux-Griffith input that could not be verified against a primary source. The range is widened to the OECD explanatory annex (Table A.4), which uses 3.29% for non-residential structures.

name: depreciation_intangibles
label: Depreciation: intangibles
description: Annual economic depreciation rate of intangibles (δ_in).
rationale: Team judgement: a standard Devereux-Griffith input that could not be verified against a primary source. The range is widened to the OECD explanatory annex (Table A.4), which uses 40.3% for acquired software.

name: profit_base_deviation_pct
label: Profit base deviation from baseline
description: Percentage error in the baseline profit base, representing receipts forecast uncertainty.
rationale: OBR Forecast evaluation report October 2024 (Table 3.1): the March 2023 forecast of 2023-24 onshore CT was £76.9bn against an outturn of £91.6bn (+19%; £10.9bn from fiscal forecasting differences). The 9.5 prior of ±5% is too narrow for such errors, so widened to normal(0, 10).

name: trend_real_growth
label: Trend real growth
description: Long-run trend real growth rate (g), used in the capital-stock law of motion.
rationale: Team judgement anchored on the OBR: trend productivity growth of 1.2% a year at the end of the November 2017 medium term, rising to 2.0% from 2030-31 in the July 2018 FSR (Box 3.1).
